definition: Avoided cost is the compensation basis regulated utilities are required to pay third-party generators (when required to purchase from them under certain rules) — equal to what the utility would have itself paid to generate that power.
core_idea: When a regulated utility is obligated to buy power from a qualifying third-party generator, it pays a price benchmarked to its own cost of self-generation, rather than a freely negotiated market price.
key_points: Applies when a utility is required to purchase power from third-party generators meeting certain requirements.
The payment equals the utility's own avoided cost of generating that power itself.
relationships: Alternative to PPAs as a mechanism for regulated utilities to source third-party generation.
trading_implications: Avoided-cost generators' revenue is benchmarked to the incumbent utility's generation cost structure, not to a competitive market price.
